title: Mastery record (one JSONL line per GLOBAL concept)
description: The learner model, keyed by globally unique concept rather than by course. Learning something once counts everywhere it is needed. State only advances on evidence recorded here; in-class success can never reach mastered, which needs a delayed retest AND a transfer test. Note the intent behind the delayed retest: it exists to CONSOLIDATE the memory, not merely to audit it, so its timing is adaptive and the minimum gaps are a floor rather than a schedule.

concept_id.description: Must exist in the global concept registry.

courses.description: Every course whose curriculum includes this concept.

state.description: unseen: not taught. introduced: taught. practiced: solved an anchored-tier item in class. consolidating: passed a delayed retest at least the minimum gap later, in a different item form. mastered: also passed a transfer test in a new setting or a cross-section combination. shaky: failed a due retest.

depth_targets.description: Different courses need the same concept to different depths: one may want can-derive where another only needs can-use. Each course states its own bar, progression inside a course is judged against that bar, and the ceiling that must not be exceeded without an explicit raise is the highest of them.

depth_reached.description: Must not exceed the highest declared target. Going deeper requires raising a target explicitly or opening a sidequest.

downstream.description: What happens to dependent concepts while this one is shaky. The default is to hold them back, but the learner may say carry on, and that decision is recorded rather than silently allowed.

hold.description: True while this concept is shaky. Dependent concepts are held back by default.

bypassed.description: Set when the learner explicitly chose to carry on anyway.

bypass_count.description: Repeated bypasses on one concept are themselves a signal and get surfaced in the progress report.

evidence.description: Append-only. Every state advance must point at entries here. Evidence earned in any course counts, because the concept is one thing.

course_id.description: Which course this evidence was earned in.

kind.description: probe: prerequisite check before a lesson. inclass: same-session practice. delayed_retest: re-asked after a gap, in a different item form, to strengthen retention. transfer_test: new setting or cross-section combination. assessment: stage exam.

latency_rating.description: How hard the recall was, not just whether it landed. Main input to the next interval: the same correct answer can deserve a very different schedule.

latency_source.description: Zep infers this by default from hesitation, rewording and hint use, and says so out loud; the learner can overrule it, which is recorded as learner_corrected.

execution_only.description: This answer showed the idea and slipped in carrying it out. Carried onto the evidence row because the state machine and the scheduler both read it: a slip does not move a concept backwards and does not shorten its next interval. Without it here, the distinction would exist in the verdict and be thrown away at the moment it matters.

scheduling.description: Adaptive review scheduling. The minimum gaps in config are a floor; the actual next date is computed from the recall history of this concept, so one that keeps slipping comes back sooner and a solid one drifts further out.

algorithm.description: Chosen in stage S1. Recorded per concept so a change of algorithm does not silently rewrite history.

next_due.description: Session open reports overdue items before any new material.

stability_days.description: Estimated days until recall probability drops to the target. FSRS style.

difficulty.description: How hard this concept is for THIS learner, estimated from their own history.

retired.description: A mastered concept recalled instantly several times running has left the review queue: the learner is using it, not maintaining it. Any answer that is not another instant pass puts it back.
